proposal.blind_spot: Current metrics show every kernel is DRAM-heavy with idle SMs, but cannot tell a truly bandwidth-saturated kernel with irreducible traffic from a latency-bound kernel with insufficient resident warps or memory-level parallelism, so the optimizer cannot choose between cutting bytes, adding occupancy/ILP, or not rewriting at all.

rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH with DRAM <90% -> latency-bound: unroll/prefetch/vectorize loads and raise parallelism instead of deleting bytes / LOW with DRAM ~90% -> genuinely bandwidth-bound: only reduce traffic, and if traffic is already minimal leave the kernel unchanged
rationale.sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustain: LOW -> occupancy too low to hide memory latency: cut registers per thread and retune num_warps/block size for more resident warps / HIGH -> occupancy is fine, confirming a pure bandwidth roofline: pursue only byte reduction or abstain from rewriting
